controls.original_statement: Record the immutable application artifact digest.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: The release record contains an approved cryptographic digest algorithm and digest that match the exact application artifact bytes.

controls.reason: For the singular application artifact bound to the assessed release, a policy-approved digest algorithm and the exact artifact bytes provide a complete objective equality check.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The release record contains an approved cryptographic digest algorithm and digest that match the exact application artifact bytes.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A substituted or modified artifact cannot pass because its freshly computed digest differs, and an absent, malformed, unapproved, or mismatched digest fails or blocks. The rule asks only to record the immutable digest, not to judge artifact quality.

controls.original_statement: Record the target deployment date and change window.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: The release record contains a valid target deployment time and ordered change-window start and end timestamps with an explicit timezone.

controls.reason: The control requires recording declared schedule facts, and valid timezone-aware target and ordered window timestamps in the release record completely satisfy that bounded requirement.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The release record contains a valid target deployment time and ordered change-window start and end timestamps with an explicit timezone.

controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing, malformed, timezone-free, or reversed timestamps cannot pass the proposed schema. Whether the chosen window is operationally wise is a separate judgment not promised by this control, so no pass-while-broken example remains within its text.

controls.original_statement: Maintain a release-specific risk register.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: An authenticated risk register exists and is bound to the assessed release identity, scope digest, and current revision.

controls.reason: The original control requires the existence of a maintained release-specific register, and the proposed authenticated record is bound to the exact release, scope digest, and current revision.

deterministic_clauses.statement: An authenticated risk register exists and is bound to the assessed release identity, scope digest, and current revision.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an empty, stale, or prior-release register: emptiness does not violate this existence-only control, while stale or wrong-release records fail the explicit binding and current-revision checks. No broader risk-quality promise is smuggled into the statement.

controls.original_statement: One authoritative source repository is identified.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: The assessed project record identifies exactly one authoritative source repository.

controls.reason: The authenticated project record is authoritative for the exact fact the rule asks for: whether one source repository is identified.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The assessed project record identifies exactly one authoritative source repository.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a project with multiple mirrors and forks. The proposal still passes only if the scoped record designates exactly one authoritative repository; mirrors do not contradict that identification, while zero or two designated authorities fail.

controls.original_statement: Protected branches prevent unreviewed direct changes.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every in-scope protected branch requires a recorded approving review before a direct change can land.
No configured branch-rule bypass permits an unreviewed direct change for the assessed principals.

controls.reason: Complete protected-branch rules and bypass settings objectively decide whether an unreviewed direct change can land.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every in-scope protected branch requires a recorded approving review before a direct change can land.
No configured branch-rule bypass permits an unreviewed direct change for the assessed principals.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an administrator push, service-account push, force push, and merge without approval. With every protected branch and principal/bypass path queried under fixed platform semantics, each unreviewed landing path fails the clauses; an unprotected branch is outside this rule's explicit subject.

controls.original_statement: Review cannot be bypassed silently by administrators.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every administrator review-bypass path emits an immutable attributable audit event.
No administrator can disable or erase review-bypass recording within the assessed repository control plane.

controls.reason: The proposal covers both attributable immutable bypass events and administrator ability to suppress those events, matching the rule's silent-bypass property.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every administrator review-bypass path emits an immutable attributable audit event.
No administrator can disable or erase review-bypass recording within the assessed repository control plane.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an administrator temporarily disabling review, using a bypass role, and deleting audit evidence. Each successful bypass must still create an immutable attributable event, and any admin ability to disable or erase recording fails the second clause, so I found no pass-while-silent case within the assessed control plane.

controls.original_statement: Merge requirements include the required automated checks.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every automated check required by the selected policy is a mandatory merge condition on each in-scope branch.

controls.reason: A versioned required-check policy plus complete in-scope branch configuration gives objective applicability and exact equality.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every automated check required by the selected policy is a mandatory merge condition on each in-scope branch.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried omitting a security check on a secondary release branch and renaming a required job. Exact policy identifiers must be mandatory on every in-scope target branch, so both cases fail rather than pass.

controls.original_statement: Changes are traceable from requirement or issue to code, review, build, artifact, and deployment.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every in-scope change links to an authenticated requirement or issue and review record.
Every in-scope change links through build provenance to an immutable artifact digest.
Every deployed in-scope artifact digest links to its deployment record.

controls.reason: Given the stated complete change inventory, immutable identifiers can mechanically prove every required traceability link in both directions.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every in-scope change links to an authenticated requirement or issue and review record.
Every in-scope change links through build provenance to an immutable artifact digest.
Every deployed in-scope artifact digest links to its deployment record.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a reviewed commit with no issue, an artifact without build provenance, and a deployment with an orphan digest. Each breaks one required join; a complete inventory prevents the checker from quietly omitting the orphan record.

controls.original_statement: Commit history and release tags are protected against unauthorized rewriting.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: All in-scope protected branches and release-tag namespaces reject rewriting by unauthorized principals.

controls.reason: Authoritative ref rules and a complete authorized-principal policy objectively determine rewriting protection for branches and release tags.

deterministic_clauses.statement: All in-scope protected branches and release-tag namespaces reject rewriting by unauthorized principals.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried force-pushing a protected branch, deleting and recreating a release tag, and using an unlisted automation identity. Each rewrite is rejected unless the principal is explicitly authorized by the versioned policy, so the clauses expose the violation.

controls.original_statement: Builds fail closed when required verification cannot run.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every verification required by the selected policy is represented in the build gate.
An unavailable, errored, or missing required verification produces a non-passing build outcome.

controls.reason: The complete required-verification inventory and explicit missing, error, and unavailable outcomes define both pass and fail behavior.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every verification required by the selected policy is represented in the build gate.
An unavailable, errored, or missing required verification produces a non-passing build outcome.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a missing job, runner outage, tool crash, and skipped required verification. Each maps to a non-passing build outcome; only verifications excluded by the selected policy fall outside applicability.

controls.original_statement: Deployable artifacts are immutable.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every deployable artifact is addressed by immutable digest and rejects replacement of content at that identity.

controls.reason: Digest addressing plus a registry mutation check objectively establishes that published artifact content cannot change at its deployable identity.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every deployable artifact is addressed by immutable digest and rejects replacement of content at that identity.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried overwriting bytes under the same digest, repointing a mutable human tag, and deleting then republishing content. Same-digest replacement must be rejected; mutable tags do not alter the digest-addressed deployable artifact, and a missing artifact cannot pass availability and mutation checks.

controls.original_statement: Every artifact has a cryptographic digest.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every in-scope artifact has a valid cryptographic digest that matches its exact bytes.

controls.reason: With a complete in-scope artifact inventory, digest syntax and exact-byte matching are fully mechanical facts.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every in-scope artifact has a valid cryptographic digest that matches its exact bytes.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an artifact with no digest, a malformed digest, and a digest calculated over different bytes. Each fails directly; there is no quality or applicability judgment once the artifact inventory is sealed.

controls.original_statement: Artifact signatures or attestations are verified before deployment.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Each deployed artifact has a valid signature or attestation under the selected trust policy.
Successful signature or attestation verification precedes the corresponding deployment event.

controls.reason: Cryptographic trust-policy verification and deployment event ordering are bounded and objectively cover the whole statement.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each deployed artifact has a valid signature or attestation under the selected trust policy.
Successful signature or attestation verification precedes the corresponding deployment event.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an invalid signature, an untrusted signer, verification after deployment, and attestation for different bytes. Each either fails the selected trust policy or the required event ordering, leaving no passing violation under the sealed artifact and deployment records.

controls.original_statement: Failed or canceled checks cannot be misrepresented as passed.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Failed, canceled, and missing required checks never produce a passed aggregate build or release status.

controls.reason: For the stated status-misrepresentation property, a fixed matrix of required job terminal states and aggregate outcomes is complete and objective.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Failed, canceled, and missing required checks never produce a passed aggregate build or release status.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried failed, canceled, timed-out, missing, and successful required jobs. The first four cannot yield a passed aggregate status under the tested mapping; a job that falsely reports its internal test as passing is a different control from misrepresenting the check's recorded terminal state.

controls.original_statement: Artifact registries enforce authentication, authorization, immutability, and retention.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every in-scope artifact registry requires authenticated access according to the selected access policy.
Every in-scope artifact registry enforces the selected authorization and immutability policy.
Every in-scope artifact registry enforces the versioned project retention policy.

controls.reason: A sealed registry inventory and versioned operation-by-role, immutability, and retention policies allow exact conformance queries.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every in-scope artifact registry requires authenticated access according to the selected access policy.
Every in-scope artifact registry enforces the selected authorization and immutability policy.
Every in-scope artifact registry enforces the versioned project retention policy.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried anonymous prohibited access, unauthorized publication, digest replacement, and early deletion. Each conflicts with one configured policy and fails its query; allowed public reads or policy-authorized deletion are not counterexamples because applicability is fixed by the selected policy.

controls.original_statement: The previous known-good artifact remains available.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: An authenticated release record identifies the previous known-good artifact digest.
The identified previous known-good artifact digest is currently retrievable from an approved registry.

controls.reason: The rule's exact fact is availability of the artifact designated previous known-good by an authenticated release record.

deterministic_clauses.statement: An authenticated release record identifies the previous known-good artifact digest.
The identified previous known-good artifact digest is currently retrievable from an approved registry.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a record with no digest, an artifact available only by mutable tag, a digest that resolves to different bytes, and a deleted digest. Each fails identification, integrity, or retrievability; whether humans selected the best artifact is outside this availability statement.

controls.original_statement: Release tags, artifacts, provenance, and deployment records agree.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Each release tag resolves to the source revision recorded in its build provenance.
Each provenance output digest equals the corresponding release artifact digest.
Each deployment record names the same artifact digest as its release artifact and provenance.

controls.reason: Complete tag, artifact, provenance, and deployment inventories can be joined by immutable revision and digest equality without interpretation.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each release tag resolves to the source revision recorded in its build provenance.
Each provenance output digest equals the corresponding release artifact digest.
Each deployment record names the same artifact digest as its release artifact and provenance.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a tag pointing to a different revision, provenance naming different bytes, an orphan deployment digest, and an extra release artifact. With all four inventories included, each creates a missing or unequal join and fails rather than passing.

controls.original_statement: Generate an SBOM for every released application artifact.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every released application artifact digest has exactly one valid bound SBOM record.

controls.reason: A complete released-application-artifact inventory and digest-bound SBOM records fully determine the generation requirement.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every released application artifact digest has exactly one valid bound SBOM record.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an omitted platform artifact, an SBOM bound to a tag instead of bytes, duplicate SBOMs, and a stale digest. The exact-one digest join fails in each case; nonapplication artifacts are objectively outside the stated scope.

controls.original_statement: Include direct and transitive components.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: The SBOM includes every direct and transitive component found in the authoritative dependency graph and final artifact inventory.

controls.reason: Given authoritative complete dependency and final-artifact graphs, direct and transitive membership comparison is mechanical.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The SBOM includes every direct and transitive component found in the authoritative dependency graph and final artifact inventory.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a lockfile transitive component omitted from the SBOM and an embedded component present only in the final artifact inventory. Each appears in one authoritative input graph and therefore makes the SBOM comparison fail.

controls.original_statement: Record exact versions, package identifiers, sources, hashes, and relationships.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every SBOM component records its exact version, package identifier, source, and hash.
Every SBOM dependency relationship matches the authoritative dependency and artifact graph.

controls.reason: Exact component fields and graph relationships are machine-verifiable against sealed package and artifact metadata.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every SBOM component records its exact version, package identifier, source, and hash.
Every SBOM dependency relationship matches the authoritative dependency and artifact graph.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a missing version, reused package identifier, wrong source, hash for different bytes, and omitted relationship edge. Each produces a direct field or graph mismatch; malformed or unavailable authoritative metadata must block rather than pass.

controls.original_statement: Link the SBOM to the released artifact digest.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Each SBOM names a subject digest equal to the digest of its exact released artifact.

controls.reason: Cryptographic digest equality between the SBOM subject and exact released bytes is a complete bounded predicate.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Each SBOM names a subject digest equal to the digest of its exact released artifact.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried binding the SBOM to a mutable tag, a source archive, a previous artifact, and a digest with the wrong algorithm value. None equals the exact released-artifact digest, so all fail.

controls.original_statement: Verify the SBOM against the final packaged artifact.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: The bound SBOM component inventory matches the complete supported inventory extracted from the final packaged artifact.

controls.reason: The proposal binds verification to the final package and requires unsupported formats to return Blocked rather than silently pass.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The bound SBOM component inventory matches the complete supported inventory extracted from the final packaged artifact.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a source-only SBOM, a missing packaged component, a supported nested archive, and an unsupported package format. Mismatches fail, supported nested content must enter the complete extracted inventory, and unsupported parsing blocks the result.

controls.original_statement: Check whether dependencies come from intended publishers and registries.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every dependency resolves from a registry allowed by the versioned project policy.
Every dependency publisher identity matches the publisher allowed by the versioned project policy and authoritative registry metadata.

controls.reason: The rule explicitly asks whether origins match intended publishers and registries, which a versioned allow policy and authoritative registry identity decide.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every dependency resolves from a registry allowed by the versioned project policy.
Every dependency publisher identity matches the publisher allowed by the versioned project policy and authoritative registry metadata.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried dependency confusion from a public registry, a namesake package from a different publisher, and a lockfile redirect. Registry allowlisting and publisher identity comparison fail each exact mismatch; intent is supplied by the approved project policy.

controls.original_statement: Continuously scan released components for newly disclosed vulnerabilities.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every supported released component remains registered with the approved vulnerability-monitoring service.
Newly disclosed vulnerability data triggers or is included within the approved maximum scan cadence for every supported release.

controls.reason: A complete supported-release inventory, authenticated monitoring registration, and approved maximum cadence make continuous coverage a bounded policy fact.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every supported released component remains registered with the approved vulnerability-monitoring service.
Newly disclosed vulnerability data triggers or is included within the approved maximum scan cadence for every supported release.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried unregistering an old supported release, delaying a new advisory beyond the cadence, and a failed scheduled scan. Each breaks registration or the maximum-cadence execution record; retired releases can be objectively excluded by the supported-release policy.

controls.original_statement: Document ownership of vendored, forked, or internally patched components.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every vendored, forked, or internally patched component in the complete inventory has a current authenticated owner record.

controls.reason: The exact requirement is a current authenticated owner record for each component in three objectively inventoried categories.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every vendored, forked, or internally patched component in the complete inventory has a current authenticated owner record.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an internally patched library hidden under a new filename, a stale owner, and a team name not present in the authority directory. Complete component classification finds the first, and record freshness/authentication rejects the latter two.

controls.original_statement: Retain SBOMs for historical releases and incident investigation.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every historical release required by the retention policy has a retrievable SBOM bound to its artifact digest.
Every incident-required SBOM remains retrievable for the incident investigation retention period.

controls.reason: Both historical-retention and active-incident promises require direct retrieval and digest verification of the SBOM artifacts; a retention registry is not artifact evidence.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every historical release required by the retention policy has a retrievable SBOM bound to its artifact digest.

At every assessment time within an active incident-investigation retention interval, the incident-required SBOM is retrievable as an artifact whose digest is bound to the exact investigated release artifact.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A structured retention record can claim that an incident SBOM is retained after the object was deleted or replaced. Direct retrieval and digest binding fail that pass-while-broken case.

controls.original_statement: Tests verify the actual artifact intended for production.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every required test result identifies an artifact digest exactly equal to the intended production artifact digest.

controls.reason: The intended production artifact and every required test result are bound by immutable digests, so exact digest equality proves the artifact identity fact stated by this control.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every required test result identifies an artifact digest exactly equal to the intended production artifact digest.

controls.counterexample_analysis: Testing a different build, a modified artifact, or a record without an artifact digest cannot pass the equality check. Test adequacy is governed by other controls; this rule asks only whether tests used the actual intended artifact.

controls.original_statement: Evidence identifies test version, data, environment, build, and result.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every test-evidence record contains test version, data-set identity, environment identity, build or artifact digest, and structured outcome.

controls.reason: The complete requirement is that evidence identifies five explicit facts, each of which is a typed record field with an objective release or artifact binding.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Every test-evidence record contains test version, data-set identity, environment identity, build or artifact digest, and structured outcome.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A record missing or malformed in any required field fails or blocks, while identical sealed records always yield the same result. The control does not ask the checker to judge whether the test itself was adequate.

controls.original_statement: A supported browser and device matrix is documented.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: The authenticated support record contains a versioned browser and device matrix with explicit versions, form factors, and policy status.

controls.reason: The control asks for documentation of an intended support policy, and an authenticated versioned matrix with explicit browser and device entries completely proves that record exists.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The authenticated support record contains a versioned browser and device matrix with explicit versions, form factors, and policy status.

controls.counterexample_analysis: Missing matrix entries, malformed versions, or an absent policy status fail the schema. Whether the chosen support set is a good market decision is outside this documentation-only control.

controls.original_statement: The required WCAG version and conformance level are documented.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: The authenticated accessibility policy records one recognized WCAG version and required conformance level for the assessed product scope.

controls.reason: The control is limited to documenting two recognized policy values, so an authenticated product-scoped record provides complete authoritative evidence of the WCAG version and level.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The authenticated accessibility policy records one recognized WCAG version and required conformance level for the assessed product scope.

controls.counterexample_analysis: An absent, unrecognized, conflicting, or unbound WCAG value fails or blocks. Determining actual conformance is a separate specialist control and is not inferred from this documentation record.

controls.original_statement: Automated accessibility scans pass within the accepted threshold.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved accessibility policy binds a scanner identity and version, scan scope, accepted severity or count threshold, and evidence freshness.
A current automated accessibility scan covers the bound scope and its normalized findings satisfy every accepted threshold.

controls.reason: The rule concerns a pinned automated scan against an accepted policy threshold, making tool identity, scope, freshness, normalized findings, and numeric comparison fully bounded.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved accessibility policy binds a scanner identity and version, scan scope, accepted severity or count threshold, and evidence freshness.
A current automated accessibility scan covers the bound scope and its normalized findings satisfy every accepted threshold.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A stale result, wrong tool version, incomplete bound scope, or finding count above threshold cannot pass. Manual accessibility quality is not claimed by this automated-scan threshold control.

controls.original_statement: Webhook retries, ordering, failure, and reconciliation are defined.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Webhook retries, ordering, failure, and reconciliation are defined.

controls.reason: The rule asks only that four webhook behaviors be defined, which an authenticated versioned contract can establish exactly.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Webhook retries, ordering, failure, and reconciliation are defined.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried omitting reconciliation, leaving failure behavior blank, and using an unversioned retry note. Each makes a required contract field absent or invalid; whether the chosen behavior is ideal is not part of this statement.

controls.original_statement: Breaking-change and deprecation policies exist.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Breaking-change and deprecation policies exist.

controls.reason: Existence of authenticated breaking-change and deprecation policy records is the complete narrow fact required.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Breaking-change and deprecation policies exist.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a release note mentioning deprecation, an expired policy, and a policy covering only breaking changes. None satisfies both current authenticated records, while policy quality is outside the rule.

controls.original_statement: Old versions have retirement dates and monitoring.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Old versions have retirement dates and monitoring.

controls.reason: With an authoritative version inventory and freshness policy, retirement dates and active monitoring are objectively queryable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Old versions have retirement dates and monitoring.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an old version without a date, a monitoring series that stopped, and an unregistered old endpoint. Complete version discovery exposes the endpoint, and each case fails the date or freshness predicate.

controls.original_statement: Common and compromised passwords are rejected where password authentication is used.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Common and compromised passwords are rejected where password authentication is used.

controls.reason: The external password corpus establishes test inputs but cannot prove application behavior; the full rejection promise requires a complete password-surface inventory and bounded rejection evidence.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved password-screening contract identifies every password enrollment, change, and recovery surface plus the exact common-password and compromised-password data sources or versions required for assessment.

Authenticated bounded execution submits representative entries from each approved common and compromised password class to every in-scope password surface and observes rejection before credential acceptance.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A checker could find a valid compromised-password list and pass while signup, reset, or password change never consults it. Exercising every sealed password surface with inputs from each approved class rejects that broken implementation.

controls.original_statement: Test, dormant, abandoned, and terminated accounts are disabled.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Test, dormant, abandoned, and terminated accounts are disabled.

controls.reason: Authoritative account lifecycle status, a complete identity inventory, and effective enabled state give an exact join.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Test, dormant, abandoned, and terminated accounts are disabled.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an enabled terminated employee, a dormant account past its approved threshold, and a test account hidden in another tenant. Complete account inventory exposes each, and enabled state conflicts with its lifecycle category.

controls.original_statement: Suspicious authentication can trigger step-up controls or investigation.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Suspicious authentication can trigger step-up controls or investigation.

controls.reason: The capability promise is bounded by the approved suspicious-event inventory and an observable outcome set, so both complete scenario coverage and actual behavior can be decided mechanically.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved suspicious-authentication scenario inventory enumerates every in-scope event type and the required step-up-control or investigation outcome for each.
Authenticated bounded execution against the assessed authentication release covers every approved suspicious event and observes at least one permitted required outcome for each event.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A policy document that merely says step-up is supported could pass while the deployed authentication path ignores every suspicious event. Requiring execution of every sealed event and an observed step-up or investigation outcome rejects that broken implementation.

controls.original_statement: Social-engineering resistance is included in support procedures.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Social-engineering resistance is included in support procedures.

controls.reason: Explicit social-engineering resistance steps in the authenticated support procedure fully satisfy this documentation requirement.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Social-engineering resistance is included in support procedures.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a generic security warning, obsolete procedure, and training-only record. None is a current support procedure containing explicit resistance steps, so each fails without needing to judge effectiveness.

controls.original_statement: A current role-permission-resource matrix exists.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: A current role-permission-resource matrix exists.

controls.reason: Existence, schema validity, version binding, and freshness of the role-permission-resource matrix are objective record facts.

deterministic_clauses.statement: A current role-permission-resource matrix exists.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a stale matrix, missing resource dimension, and unsigned spreadsheet. Each fails the named schema or freshness/authentication policy; whether permissions are wise is outside this existence rule.

controls.original_statement: Temporary permissions expire automatically.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Temporary permissions expire automatically.

controls.reason: Temporary-grant expiry and current effective access are authoritative timestamp and state facts.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Temporary permissions expire automatically.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a grant with no expiry, an expired grant still effective through a group, and a delayed cleanup. Effective-access resolution after the policy deadline catches each; mere expiry metadata without revocation cannot pass.

controls.original_statement: Emergency access is time-bounded and reviewed.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Emergency access is time-bounded and reviewed.

controls.reason: The two promises, time bounding and review, are objective only when the maximum duration, review deadline, complete grant inventory, runtime expiry, and grant-bound reviews are all checked.

Every emergency-access grant whose review deadline has passed has an authenticated review record bound to that exact grant and reviewer identity.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A grant record with an expiry field could pass while the credential still works after expiry, or a generic quarterly review could exist without reviewing that grant. The environment expiry check and per-grant review join reject both cases.

controls.original_statement: Concurrent-session policy is defined.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Concurrent-session policy is defined.

controls.reason: The statement asks only for a current concurrent-session policy record, so authenticated existence and version binding are complete.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Concurrent-session policy is defined.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an informal wiki note, a policy with no effective date, and a record missing concurrent-session behavior. Each fails the record schema or freshness predicate; the chosen number of sessions is not judged.

controls.original_statement: Allowed types are explicitly listed.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Allowed types are explicitly listed.

controls.reason: Presence of a parseable explicit allowed-type list is the complete narrow fact required by this rule.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Allowed types are explicitly listed.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried relying only on blocked types, prose examples, and runtime inference. None is an explicit exhaustive allowlist, while the checker need not judge whether the chosen allowed types are safe.

controls.original_statement: User-provided filenames are not used as trusted filesystem paths.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: User-provided filenames are not used as trusted filesystem paths.

controls.reason: With complete supported path data flow and Unknown yielding Blocked, user filename influence on trusted path construction is mechanically decidable.

deterministic_clauses.statement: User-provided filenames are not used as trusted filesystem paths.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried direct concatenation, normalized traversal, and using the filename after storage indirection. Any tainted filename reaching a trusted filesystem-path sink fails; applications that generate internal opaque paths and retain the name only as metadata pass legitimately.

controls.original_statement: Abandoned, failed, and orphaned uploads are cleaned up.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Abandoned, failed, and orphaned uploads are cleaned up.

controls.reason: Defined terminal states, age thresholds, complete upload records, and current storage queries make cleanup status objective.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Abandoned, failed, and orphaned uploads are cleaned up.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a failed upload past its deadline, an abandoned multipart upload, and an object with no owning record. Each is classified by the policy and remains queryable, so its continued existence fails.

controls.original_statement: Certificates cover the correct names and trust chains.

old_deterministic_clauses.statement: Certificates cover the correct names and trust chains.
